The core insight of the paper lies in distinguishing between possession quantity and possession quality through a dual-layer approach. The event layer computes a normalized possession value (q(s)) based on expected threat gain, expected goals, and box touches, effectively capturing on-ball value. Sequences with q(s) below a threshold (0.15) are flagged as 'junk'. This provides a proxy for sterile possession. The spatial layer introduces the Space Creation Index (SCI), which quantifies how much an offensive sequence moves the defense by measuring changes in attacking third control and opponent presence in their own attacking zone. This is modeled using a pitch-control framework. The combination of these layers allows for a nuanced understanding of whether possession creates meaningful space or is merely dead. The sterile index aggregates these insights into a single scalar measure that penalizes high possession percentages paired with low efficiency. In GSE, this translates to a probabilistic model where EPA and spatial metrics jointly inform offensive state transitions, enabling real-time prediction of outcome-relevant variance missed by traditional on-ball metrics.
